summary:
TerraMind AI finds places on Earth whose terrain matches future landing and base sites on the Moon and Mars. Mission teams rehearse on Earth, but “this place looks like the Moon” is usually judged by eye. We turn it into a measured, repeatable number.

We measure slope, relief and roughness from NASA elevation data (LRO LOLA for the Moon, MOLA for Mars, SRTM for Earth) on one common 463 m grid and compare them. A person approves every reference window before any score exists. The platform scans whole regions of Earth, shows ranked candidates on a map, compares Moon/Mars and Earth surfaces side by side in 3D, adds a landing-slope screen, and produces a one-page brief with sources. An AI assistant explains results in any language; every number it states is checked against the computed results.

The method recognises known Mars analogs (Atacama, Utah) and found new candidates in Uzbekistan for Mons Mouton, an Artemis III region. It is open source.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

TerraMind AI turns “does this place on Earth look like that place on the Moon or Mars?” into a measured, reviewable number, and searches whole regions of Earth for new analog sites.

HOW IT WORKS

1. Reference sites: Mons Mouton Plateau on the Moon (an Artemis III candidate region), Gale crater floor (Curiosity) and Meridiani Planum (Opportunity) on Mars.

2. Each site gets a 25 x 25 km window in its own local projection (Moon sphere R = 1,737,400 m, Mars sphere R = 3,396,190 m, Earth WGS84).

3. Every elevation model is brought to one 463 m grid. We compute slope (Horn method), local relief and roughness (Terrain Ruggedness Index).

4. Similarity is the overlap of these distributions (0 = none, 1 = identical). Two weight sets are reported to show the ranking does not depend on the weights.

5. Human review gate: a person approves each window before any score is computed; changing a window afterwards blocks scoring.

6. Analog Finder: the same window slides across a region of Earth (NASA SRTM). Lakes and seas are excluded. Top candidates go to human review on satellite imagery.

7. Platform: choose Mars or the Moon, click a point on the LOLA south-pole map, scan Earth, and compare both surfaces side by side in 3D on one scale. A landing screen shows the share of each window flatter than 5 and 15 degrees. Every candidate has a one-page brief with numbers, sources and review state.
